results-published.name: The build published its test results
results-published.description: The build left a readable test report naming at least as many cases as the team expects, instead of reporting nothing at all.
results-published.remediation:
Before `buildnote guardrails` runs, write the test reports your test runner already produces into the workspace, and keep them there. Gradle writes JUnit XML to `build/test-results/`, and most runners take a flag:

```bash
./gradlew test
pytest --junitxml=junit.xml
dotnet test --logger trx
```

A missing report is the violation. If a pipeline's test step went green but left nothing behind, you can't show it ran a single test, and a report with no test cases is the same thing. If a job genuinely has no tests, leave the guardrail off for that job instead of lowering `minTests` to zero.

minTests.description: Fewest test cases the reports must contain in total. A report with no cases doesn't count as a test run.

no-failures.name: No test failed or errored
no-failures.description: Every test case in the reports passed or was skipped, so no failing test gets past the gate.
no-failures.remediation:
Fix the failing tests, or delete the ones that no longer describe how the system behaves. A test that stays red stops being read, and the next real failure hides behind it.

Reproduce a single test case before pushing:

```bash
./gradlew test --tests 'com.company.widget.QueueTest'
```

If a test fails because it's flaky, not because the code is wrong, quarantine it in the test framework so the quarantine can be reviewed next to the test. Turning off the guardrail makes the same decision somewhere nobody looks.

coverage-floor.name: Coverage is at or above the floor
coverage-floor.description: The coverage the build measured is at or above the line and branch floors the team sets. Both floors default to zero, so the guardrail just reports the number until the team chooses one.

minLines.description: Lowest line coverage percentage that passes, `0` for no floor. Only checked when the reports measured lines at all.

minBranches.description: Lowest branch coverage percentage that passes, `0` for no floor. Ignored when the reports contain no branch data, whether because the project has no branches or because the format omits them.

no-skipped-growth.name: Skipped tests stay within budget
no-skipped-growth.description: The reports contain no more skipped cases than the budget allows. The budget is a fixed number in the configuration, not a comparison with the previous build, so it only catches growth if the team lowers the number as skipped tests come back.

maxSkipped.description: Maximum number of cases the reports may mark as skipped, ignored or inconclusive.
